chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Dawud al-Khandaqi from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you stand in prayer, know that you are before Allah. If you do not see Him, know that He sees you. So face your prayer, do not spit, do not blow your nose, do not break your fingers, and do not twist your body, for a people were punished for breaking their fingers and twisting their bodies in prayer. When you raise your head from bowing, keep your back straight until your joints return to place. And when you prostrate, do the same. And when you are in the first and second rak'ah and raise your head from prostration, sit still until your joints return to place. When you rise, say:

key_terms.بِحَوْلِ اللَّهِ وَقُوَّتِهِ: With the power and strength of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended physical etiquettes and prohibitions during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the precise physical etiquette (adab) of prayer, linking ritual correctness to spiritual mindfulness by reminding the worshipper that although God is unseen, He is all-seeing. It specifically prohibits distracting acts like spitting or twisting fingers, citing historical precedents of punishment for such negligence, and prescribes the supplication 'Bi-hawli Allahi wa quwwatihi' upon rising, a practice attributed to Imam Ali (AS). This emphasizes the Shia scholarly view that external precision in movement reflects internal devotion and adherence to the Prophetic tradition.
